product.name: XbotGo AI sports tracking camera with handheld remote
product.category: AI auto-tracking sports camera / motorised pan mount
product.summary: Lime-green soft-touch body with a built-in wide-angle camera, dark grey end caps printed 'XbotGo', a rotating round base and a clamp-style holder on top, plus a separate grey key remote marked 'Xbot'. Only the exterior is shown, so every internal part (boards, cells, motor, chips) is inferred or assumed from the product class. Scale is estimated by assuming the lens bezel is about 40 mm wide; the main unit is taken as roughly 96 x 68 x 147 mm and the remote as 40 x 12 x 86 mm.
product.powerInput: Assumed USB-C, 5 V up to 2 A, charging an internal Li-ion pack; remote assumed to run on a CR2032 coin cell

parts.name: Front housing half (green soft-touch)
parts.function: Carries the lens bezel, front button, mic port and LED light pipes.
parts.evidence: Lime-green rounded body visible from the front, matte finish suggesting silicone or TPE overmould.
parts.unknowns: Whether the green is a removable sleeve or a bonded overmould; pull at an edge to check.

parts.name: Rear housing half
parts.function: Closes the body and holds the battery pack and charging port.
parts.evidence: Green body wraps to the rear; a mating half is needed to assemble the internals.
parts.unknowns: Actual split line location and rear features are not visible.

parts.name: Dark grey side cap with XbotGo logo
parts.function: Cosmetic end caps that hide housing screws and act as RF windows.
parts.evidence: Dark panel with white 'XbotGo' logo visible on the right side; the left one is assumed symmetrical.

parts.name: Lens bezel and cover glass
parts.function: Protects the lens and trims the camera opening.
parts.evidence: Grey squircle fascia with concentric rings around a glass lens on the upper front.

parts.name: Wide-angle camera module
parts.function: Captures the video used for recording and AI tracking.
parts.evidence: Large lens visible on the front; the sensor and lens barrel must sit behind it.
parts.unknowns: Sensor type and resolution; read the marking on the sensor flex or board.

parts.name: Main processor board
parts.function: Hosts the vision processor, memory, radio, power management and motor drive.
parts.evidence: An AI tracking camera needs a multilayer processor board; none is visible.

parts.name: AI vision processor
parts.function: Runs video encoding and the tracking neural network, and commands the pan motor.
parts.evidence: On-device tracking of this kind needs an SoC with an ISP and an NPU.
parts.unknowns: Exact part; open the unit and read the top mark, possibly under a shield or thermal pad.

parts.name: LPDDR memory
parts.function: Working memory for the processor.
parts.evidence: Typical for a Linux-class vision SoC.

parts.name: eMMC flash storage
parts.function: Stores firmware and recorded video.
parts.evidence: Typical for the product class; it may be a microSD slot instead or as well.

parts.name: Power management IC
parts.function: Generates the 3.3 V, 1.8 V and core rails from the battery and handles the power key.
parts.evidence: A multi-rail SoC needs a PMIC or several buck converters.

parts.name: Wi-Fi / Bluetooth module
parts.function: Links to the phone app over Wi-Fi and to the remote over Bluetooth LE.
parts.evidence: A wireless remote is shown and the product is app-controlled, so a 2.4 GHz radio is required.
parts.unknowns: Whether the remote uses BLE or a proprietary 2.4 GHz link; check the FCC ID filing.

parts.name: 2.4/5 GHz FPC antenna
parts.function: Radiates Wi-Fi and Bluetooth through the plastic side cap.
parts.evidence: The plastic side caps are the natural RF window; the location is a guess.

parts.name: Three-phase gimbal motor driver
parts.function: Drives the pan motor windings from battery voltage.
parts.evidence: The body rotates on its base to track, so a motor and driver are required.

parts.name: 6-axis IMU
parts.function: Senses body motion for stabilisation and position feedback.
parts.evidence: Typical in motorised tracking mounts.

parts.name: Decoupling capacitors and passives
parts.function: Rail decoupling, pull-ups and filtering around the ICs.
parts.evidence: Always present on a board of this type.

parts.name: Front UI daughterboard
parts.function: Carries the front button switch, four battery LEDs and the microphone.
parts.evidence: Button, pinhole and four green LEDs sit in a vertical line on the lower front, away from where a main board would be.
parts.unknowns: Could be a flex circuit or part of the main board.

parts.name: Front button cap
parts.function: User power / function key.
parts.evidence: Grey pill-shaped button with a ring mark below the lens.

parts.name: Tact switch (front button)
parts.function: Converts the button press to a signal for the power controller.
parts.evidence: A switch must sit behind the visible button cap.

parts.name: Green battery level LEDs
parts.function: Show the charge level and status.
parts.evidence: Four small green dots in a row near the bottom of the front face.

parts.name: MEMS microphone
parts.function: Records audio with the video.
parts.evidence: Small pinhole above the front button is most likely a mic port; it could instead be a status LED.

parts.name: Li-ion cells (18650, pack of two)
parts.function: Powers the camera and motor for a multi-hour game.
parts.evidence: The body volume and a four-LED gauge suggest an internal pack; cell count and format are guesses.
parts.unknowns: Series or parallel, capacity and protection circuit; read the pack label after opening.

parts.name: Charging / power board
parts.function: Holds the USB-C port, charger and battery protection.
parts.evidence: A rear charging port needs a board near the back wall; no port is visible in the photo.

parts.name: USB-C charging port
parts.function: Charging input and possibly data.
parts.evidence: Not visible; typical for a current rechargeable camera.
parts.unknowns: Location and whether it supports USB PD; inspect the rear and the rating label.

parts.name: Battery charger IC
parts.function: Charges the pack from 5 V USB (boost charger if the pack is 2S).
parts.evidence: Required by a USB-charged Li-ion pack.

parts.name: Charger power inductor
parts.function: Energy storage for the switching charger.
parts.evidence: A switching charger needs an inductor.

parts.name: Brushless pan motor with encoder
parts.function: Rotates the body on the base to follow the action.
candidates: Hollow-shaft gimbal BLDC with magnetic encoder
parts.evidence: The body sits on a separate round base with a visible gap, typical of a pan axis.
parts.unknowns: Motor type and whether there is a second (tilt) axis; rotate by hand and feel for cogging or gear noise.

parts.name: Rotating base / mount foot
parts.function: Stationary foot that the body pans on; probably has a tripod thread or magnet underneath.
parts.material: Die-cast or machined aluminium ring with plastic cover
parts.evidence: Dark grey round foot with a metallic lower ring under the green body.
parts.unknowns: Underside mounting (1/4-inch thread, magnet or quick-release) is not visible.

parts.name: Top swivel neck
parts.function: Joins the top holder to the body and lets it turn.
parts.evidence: Grey stepped stem between the body and the top arm.

parts.name: Top holder / clamp arm
parts.function: Appears to be a folding holder on top, most likely a spring clamp for a phone or accessory.
parts.material: PC+ABS with silicone pad, steel spring
parts.evidence: Grey rounded bar with a green padded part behind it on top of the neck.
parts.unknowns: Exact purpose (phone clamp, handle or antenna); open and close it to see.

parts.name: Housing screws
parts.function: Hold the front and rear halves together.
parts.evidence: No screws are visible; they are probably hidden under the side caps or the skin.

parts.name: Remote top shell
parts.function: Key-side housing of the remote.
parts.evidence: Grey pill-shaped remote with 'Xbot' printed at the bottom.

parts.name: Remote bottom shell with battery door
parts.function: Closes the remote and holds the coin cell.
parts.evidence: A mating half is required; the back is not visible.

parts.name: Remote PCB
parts.function: Carries the key contacts, the radio chip and a printed antenna.
parts.evidence: Seven keys on a slim wireless remote imply a single board behind them.

parts.name: Remote direction keys
parts.function: Manually steer the camera up, down, left and right.
parts.evidence: Four arrow marks around a circular pad on the remote.

parts.name: Remote centre key
parts.function: Centre key with a circular-arrow icon, likely re-centre or auto-tracking.
parts.evidence: Round key with a rotate/target icon in the middle of the direction pad.

parts.name: Remote power key
parts.function: Power key with the standby symbol.
parts.evidence: Round key with a power icon at lower left of the remote.

parts.name: Remote record key
parts.function: Starts and stops recording.
parts.evidence: Round key with a red dot at lower right of the remote.

parts.name: Remote dome switches
parts.function: Contact closures under each remote key.
parts.package: Metal dome or carbon pill contact
parts.evidence: Seven keys need seven contacts.

parts.name: Remote 2.4 GHz radio SoC
parts.function: Scans the keys and sends commands to the camera.
parts.evidence: A wireless remote without a visible IR window most likely uses Bluetooth LE.
parts.unknowns: BLE, proprietary 2.4 GHz or IR; check for an IR LED at the top edge and read the chip mark.

parts.name: Remote coin cell
parts.function: Powers the remote.
parts.evidence: Slim remote of this size typically uses a CR2032; it could be a small rechargeable cell.

unknowns: Nothing inside is visible: all boards, chips, cells and the motor are inferred or assumed from the exterior and the product class.
Battery configuration (2S 18650, 1S2P or pouch) and capacity; read the rating label or the pack.
Charging port type and location; the back and underside are not shown.
Whether there is a second motorised axis (tilt) or only pan.
Purpose of the top arm: phone clamp, handle or accessory holder.
Whether the pinhole above the front button is a microphone or a status LED.
Remote link technology (BLE, proprietary 2.4 GHz or IR) and its battery type.
Base mounting interface (1/4-inch thread, magnet, quick release).
All dimensions are scaled from an assumed 40 mm lens bezel and may be off by 20 percent or more.
verifySteps: Photograph the rear, underside and rating label to confirm the charging port, input rating and mounting thread.
Look up the FCC ID on the label for internal photos and the radio types of the camera and remote.
Measure the main unit and the remote with callipers to correct the scale.
Remove the side caps and open the housing; photograph both sides of each board and read the IC markings.
Read the battery pack label for chemistry, voltage and capacity, and measure pack voltage.
Rotate the body on the base by hand and operate the top arm to identify the motorised axes and the arm's function.
Open the remote battery door to confirm the cell type and scan for a BLE advertisement when a key is pressed.
Measure USB input current during charging with an inline meter.
safety: Contains lithium-ion cells (assumed): do not puncture, short or pry against the pack when opening; disconnect the battery first.
The pan motor can start unexpectedly when powered; keep fingers and cables clear of the base gap.
A coin cell in the remote is a swallowing hazard; keep away from children.
Soft-touch skin and adhesive-fixed caps can tear; use plastic tools and gentle heat.
